question: Beckwith-Wieddeman Syndrome.. Beckwith-Wieddeman Syndrome. I would like to request further knowledge on this specific disorder
answer:
Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a condition that affects many parts of the body and is classified as an overgrowth syndrome [2]. Affected infants are typically larger than normal (macrosomia) and may have uneven growth, such as hemihyperplasia, which often becomes less noticeable with age [2]. The disorder affects about 1 in 13,700 newborns worldwide, though it might be more common because some cases with mild symptoms go undiagnosed [4].

The condition can sometimes run in families and may follow an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance, meaning one copy of a changed gene is enough to cause the disorder. In about 85% of cases, only one family member has been diagnosed; however, parents of a child with this syndrome have a risk for having other children affected [1].

The sources listed do not cover specific treatments or management strategies in detail beyond mentioning diagnostic tests and genetic counseling as part of care [3]. For personalized medical advice, consult a healthcare professional.
